edges.description: Colonizing bacteria attach to host or device surfaces and initiate matrix-protected biofilm communities.
edges.source: Environmental A. baumannii Exposure and Colonization

edges.description: Protected colonizing populations deliver surface and vesicle-associated virulence factors, including OmpA, to epithelial and immune cells.
Biofilm-protected colonization of wounds and devices produces local skin and soft-tissue infection.
OmpA-dependent epithelial and macrophage injury amplifies pulmonary inflammation, damages lung tissue, and can help bacteria disseminate systemically.
Inflammatory lung injury and alveolar barrier breach present clinically as Acinetobacter pneumonia.
Severe nosocomial pneumonia can progress to bloodstream infection, septic shock, and organ failure.
Bloodstream infection manifests clinically as bacteremic sepsis.
Hematogenous seeding can produce infective endocarditis.
Ventilation and invasive devices create healthcare contact and mucosal access points through which MDR A. baumannii can colonize the patient.
